info.title: Big Batch OCR API
info.description: HTTP API for submitting and tracking OCR batch jobs. Inputs may be uploaded as a tar.gz archive; directory-based submissions are disabled by default and require ALLOW_DIRECTORY_ACCESS=true. Successful output directories can be downloaded by job ID as tar.gz. All directory paths are relative to the API host's configured data root. The API runs the configured OCR container; callers cannot provide arbitrary mounts, Docker options, OCRmyPDF arguments, or host paths. Only the validated language and optimization settings are configurable per job. Optional completion webhooks POST the final job status and include the configured rootPath in the JSON body; they may also include X-Webhook-Secret and X-Root-Path headers. The `/api/v1` URL prefix identifies the major API version. Backward-compatible additions remain in v1; breaking contract changes require a new major URL version.

post.description: Submits an OCR job in the requested mode. Optional language and optimize values override the API host's OCR_LANGUAGE and OCR_OPTIMIZE defaults for this job. An optional webhookUrl receives one POST with the final job status after the job reaches a terminal state. webhookSecret and rootPath are optional and require webhookUrl; they are sent as X-Webhook-Secret and X-Root-Path headers, respectively, and rootPath is also included as a rootPath property in the webhook JSON body. Webhook delivery is best-effort, with one request attempt and no retry; callback failures are logged and do not change the job outcome. Synchronous mode waits for the container to finish and returns the resulting tar.gz archive directly, with the job ID in the X-Job-ID response header. Asynchronous mode acknowledges the job and returns a URL for polling its status. Jobs are queued when the configured concurrency limit is reached. A client disconnect or client-side timeout does not cancel an accepted job; use asynchronous mode when the client cannot wait for completion, and poll the returned status URL rather than resubmitting. If the server's synchronous wait limit is reached, it returns 504 with the accepted job ID and status URL; the job continues. Job metadata is persisted so a host restart cannot report unfinished work as successful.

createMissingDestination.summary: Explicitly create a missing destination directory

200.description: Synchronous job completed successfully; the response body is its processed output archive.

202.description: Asynchronous job accepted. The status is a snapshot and may already be terminal by the time the response reaches the client.

Location.description: URL of the job status resource.

413.description: The request body exceeds its size limit: 1 GiB for multipart requests and 1 MiB for JSON requests.

403.description: Directory-based submissions are disabled by configuration. Upload an inputArchive instead.

500.description: The OCR execution failed. The response identifies the failed job; its status can also be retrieved using the provided URL.

504.description: The synchronous wait limit was reached. The accepted job continues; poll its status URL instead of submitting it again.

example.title: Synchronous wait limit exceeded
example.detail: The job is still running and was not cancelled.

post.description: Cleans up only succeeded, failed, or cancelled jobs. Active jobs are ignored and reported in `activeJobsSkipped`. Scope `uploads` deletes metadata and private workspaces for jobs submitted with uploaded archives. Scope `all` also deletes each terminal shared-directory job's whole input and output directories, except paths shared with active jobs or containing API host database files. Unsafe or unresolvable terminal paths are preserved and reported in `jobsSkippedForUnsafePaths`. Shared-directory cleanup is destructive and permanent.

all.summary: Remove all terminal job data, including shared directories

200.description: Cleanup completed. Active jobs and terminal jobs whose paths are needed by active jobs are ignored, not treated as errors. Unsafe or unresolvable terminal paths are preserved and reported in the result.

500.description: A data path could not be safely resolved or removed.

get.description: Returns the latest persisted state and outcome for a submitted job. A failed job is returned as a job resource with status `failed`; this is distinct from an HTTP error retrieving the resource. If the host restarts while work is unfinished, the API must not report it as successful unless completion was confirmed.

200.description: Current job state and available completion details.

queued.summary: Job waiting for an available worker

delete.description: Deletes the persisted job record, including its stored container logs and outcome metadata. For jobs submitted with an uploaded archive, also removes the private input/output workspace. Jobs must already be terminal; cancel queued or running jobs first and wait for cancellation to finish. Caller-provided shared input and output directories are never deleted.

204.description: The terminal job record and any uploaded-job workspace were deleted.

409.description: The job is queued, starting, running, or cancelling. Cancel it and wait until it reaches a terminal state before deletion.

500.description: The job record or uploaded-job workspace could not be deleted.

post.description: Cancels a queued job immediately. For a starting or running job, requests cancellation of its managed OCR container and returns while the container is being stopped. Poll the job status URL until the terminal `cancelled` state is recorded. Cancellation does not delete job data; use the job DELETE or cleanup endpoint to remove it.

200.description: A queued job was cancelled immediately, or the job was already cancelled.

202.description: Cancellation was requested for a starting or running job; the managed container is being stopped.

409.description: The job already succeeded or failed and cannot be cancelled.

500.description: The cancellation request could not be persisted.

post.summary: Resume a failed or cancelled OCR job
post.description: Requeues the existing job using its current job ID, stored input and output paths, and OCR settings. The previous attempt's start/completion timestamps, exit code, error, container ID, and logs are cleared. Resumed jobs are added to the end of the queue. Only jobs with status `failed` or `cancelled` can be resumed.

202.description: The job was accepted for retry.

Location.description: URL for polling the resumed job's status.

409.description: The job exists but is not failed or cancelled.

example.title: Job cannot be resumed
example.detail: Only failed or cancelled jobs can be resumed.

500.description: The resume request could not be persisted.

get.description: Downloads all files in the job's output directory as a tar.gz archive. The result is available only after the job reaches `succeeded`. The archive is generated when requested; downloading does not remove job data and results may be downloaded repeatedly. Use the job DELETE or cleanup endpoint to explicitly remove uploaded-job workspaces.

410.description: The uploaded job's private workspace is no longer available, for example because it was removed outside the API.

example.title: Job result unavailable
example.detail: The uploaded job workspace is no longer present on the data volume.

500.description: The output directory could not be packaged for download.

get.description: Unauthenticated liveness endpoint. It reports whether the API process is responsive; it does not guarantee that Docker or OCR execution is available.

BearerAuth.description: Send the configured API key as a bearer token in the Authorization header. Key-based authentication is required by default; the host must fail startup if this mode is enabled without a key. Omitting the key is accepted only when the host operator explicitly enables unauthenticated access in host configuration.

JobId.name: jobId
JobId.description: Identifier returned when the job was submitted.

scope.description: `uploads` removes uploaded-archive workspaces and metadata only. `all` also removes whole shared input/output directories for terminal jobs.

jobsDeleted.description: Number of terminal job records deleted.

activeJobsSkipped.description: Number of queued, starting, running, or cancelling jobs left untouched.

jobsSkippedForActiveData.description: Number of terminal jobs whose shared directories overlap paths referenced by active jobs.

jobsSkippedForServerData.description: Number of terminal jobs skipped because their directory contains the API host database.

jobsSkippedForUnsafePaths.description: Number of terminal jobs preserved because one or more recorded directories no longer resolve safely.

inputPath.description: Input directory relative to the configured data root. It must resolve to an existing, readable directory and is accepted only when ALLOW_DIRECTORY_ACCESS=true.

outputPath.description: Destination directory relative to the configured data root. It must already exist unless `createDestination` is true.

mode.description: Synchronous mode waits for completion. Asynchronous mode returns an acknowledgement and a status URL.

createDestination.description: When true, the host may create the missing destination directory, and any missing parent directories, only beneath the configured data root. When omitted or false, a missing destination is rejected.

language.description: Optional OCRmyPDF language code or '+'-separated codes, such as 'eng' or 'deu+eng'. Defaults to the API host's OCR_LANGUAGE.

optimize.description: Optional OCRmyPDF optimization level. Defaults to the API host's OCR_OPTIMIZE.

webhookUrl.description: Optional absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL that receives a POST with the final job resource as JSON. Redirects are not followed.

webhookSecret.description: Optional value sent in the X-Webhook-Secret callback header. Requires webhookUrl.

rootPath.description: Optional automation destination root path included as rootPath in the webhook JSON body and sent in the X-Root-Path callback header. Requires webhookUrl.

SubmitMultipartJobRequest.description: Send the form fields as multipart/form-data. Include exactly one input source: inputPath for the shared-directory workflow (requires ALLOW_DIRECTORY_ACCESS=true), inputArchive as a .tar.gz file part, inputArchiveContents as raw .tar.gz bytes in a multipart text field, or inputArchiveContentsBase64 as standard Base64-encoded .tar.gz bytes in a multipart text field. For archive uploads, omit inputPath and outputPath: the API creates a private workspace named for the job ID with separate input and output directories. The workspace is retained after downloads and cancellation until removed through the job DELETE or cleanup endpoint. The complete request body is limited to 1 GiB and extracted archive contents to 10 GiB. Archive entries must be regular files or directories; links and paths escaping the archive root are rejected.

inputPath.description: Existing readable input directory beneath the data root; mutually exclusive with all archive fields and accepted only when ALLOW_DIRECTORY_ACCESS=true.

inputArchive.description: A .tar.gz file containing the input files; mutually exclusive with inputPath. When present, omit outputPath; the API creates an isolated per-job input/output workspace that remains until explicitly removed with the job DELETE or cleanup endpoint.

inputArchiveContents.description: Raw .tar.gz bytes in a multipart text field, for integrations such as Workato's Compress files action that expose archive contents rather than a file object. Mutually exclusive with inputArchive and inputPath.

inputArchiveContentsBase64.description: Standard Base64-encoded .tar.gz bytes in a multipart text field. Mutually exclusive with all other input sources. The API validates and decodes this value before extracting the archive.

language.description: Optional OCRmyPDF language code or '+'-separated codes, such as 'eng' or 'deu+eng'. Defaults to OCR_LANGUAGE.

optimize.description: Optional OCRmyPDF optimization level. Defaults to OCR_OPTIMIZE.

webhookUrl.description: Optional absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL that receives a POST with the final job resource as JSON. Redirects are not followed.

webhookSecret.description: Optional value sent in the X-Webhook-Secret callback header. Requires webhookUrl.

rootPath.description: Optional automation destination root path sent in the X-Root-Path callback header. Requires webhookUrl.

jobId.description: Stable identifier for this accepted job.

statusUrl.description: Relative URL to poll for the persisted job state.

JobLifecycleStatus.description: `succeeded`, `failed`, and `cancelled` are terminal states. `cancelling` means a running job's managed container is being stopped.

inputPath.description: Submitted path relative to the configured data root.

outputPath.description: Submitted path relative to the configured data root.

startedAt.description: Present after the job begins starting.

completedAt.description: Present after the job reaches a terminal state.

exitCode.description: OCR container exit code, available when execution has finished.

error.description: Safe, client-facing failure information for a failed job; null until a failure is recorded.

message.description: Safe summary that does not expose secrets, host paths, or internal container configuration.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details with a stable API-specific code.

BadRequest.description: Malformed JSON, invalid request shape, or OCR options that do not satisfy the documented language and optimization constraints.

example.title: Invalid request
example.detail: The request body is not valid for this operation.

Unauthorized.description: Bearer key is missing or invalid. Credentials are never returned in error responses.

example.title: Unauthorized
example.detail: A valid bearer API key is required.

InvalidPath.description: A path is invalid, outside the configured data root, unreadable, or does not meet the required directory existence rules. Path validation happens before a job is started.

example.title: Invalid path
example.detail: The input directory must be a readable directory beneath the configured data root.

PathConflict.description: Input and destination resolve to the same directory or incompatible nested directories.

example.title: Incompatible directories
example.detail: Input and destination directories must be distinct and must not contain one another.

JobNotFound.description: No job with this identifier is available to the authenticated caller.

example.title: Job not found
example.detail: No job was found for the supplied identifier.

JobNotCompleted.description: The job exists, but its output archive is available only after successful completion.

example.title: Job result unavailable
example.detail: The processed files are available only after the job succeeds.
